entry.title: 24 Oct: we re-checked the 31 projects we last graded between 6 and 12 Oct against their current code: 31 keep their grade (1 after a full re-read). 24 Oct: the project left from the 23 Oct re-check, acamilo-flybrain, keeps its grade C after a full re-read. brainlab keeps A after a full re-read: on 23 Oct 2026 the author added a report that records a failed check of a different result, whether the real wiring helps the frozen olfactory circuit integrate angular velocity (the real wiring did no better than a no-information guess); the first-campaign report its grade cites did not change.

202 catalogue entries (24 Oct 2026): 2 new: somahouse A (helps): from the author's committed held-out results (60 test scenarios, 3 training seeds; not re-run by us), the fly-derived circuit cost 0.1589 against 0.1622 for a degree-preserving rewired copy (lower is better), but dense wiring (0.1538) and a conventional controller with no brain (0.1172) both cost less than the fly wiring. fly-trader A (no difference): from the author's committed matched comparison (3 seeds, 10 unseen tickers; not re-run by us), the excess return over buy-and-hold (the no-brain baseline, 0 by definition) was +280.3 points with the FlyWire circuit against +211.0 with a random-weight circuit of the same size (paired difference +69.3, 95% interval -186.6 to +325.3). fly-chess keeps B, and its wiring result is now worse: the author committed a shuffled-wiring control, and under the same readout probe the shuffled brain scored higher than the real one (20.9% against 18.0% top-1; board-blind 11.7%; on the author's Elo ladder 682 against 653 and 631). Only a readout is trained on the frozen connectome. Odyssey-3 claim: No method, code or write-up was published as of 24 Oct 2026; no public fly mode found on the preview page (24 Oct).

Controls ledger (24 Oct 2026): 3 new rows (somahouse helps, fly-trader no difference, fly-chess worse), now 94 studies, 84 with a wiring null: helps 33, no difference 24, worse 9, mixed 15, not yet scored 3; fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 33 of 84. Scoring unchanged.

neural-canvas browser check (24 Oct 2026): 24 Oct: in a headless browser without a GPU, after we pressed 'Download & start', the page downloaded about 77 MB of connectome data within 82 seconds and started a background worker, and the picture kept changing in our screenshots after that. Screenshots cannot show whether the brain drives the movement. Our screenshot requests timed out from about 143 seconds after the click, so we have no picture of the page for the rest of our watch. We identified the connectome files by their web address, a method we fixed before this check. The page's own status line read "JavaScript · 0.08× realtime · 0 spikes". In our browser checks of 3, 6, 11, 17, 18, 20, 22 and 24 Oct 2026, 8 of 13 demos ran by our check's rule on a machine without a GPU at their latest check. neural-canvas is not counted among them: our check's rule marks a page as unresponsive when its screenshot requests fail, and on 24 Oct our screenshot requests timed out from about 143 seconds after the click, so we have no picture of the page for the rest of our watch.

New plain answer on Is it real?: Is the fruit fly brain open source? From the licence facts already on our pages (FlyWire CC BY-NC 4.0 by our stricter reading vs CC BY 4.0 on its Zenodo record; code licences per project).

Tracking (24 Oct 2026): 143 tracked repositories checked on 24 Oct 2026: 138 unchanged, 2 already gone, 3 changed (among them flybench, whose new commit will be checked against its grade in the next run); no new broken links; 56 of 56 videos available. View counts: 12 of the 56 videos were refreshed from YouTube search pages on 24 Oct 2026 (approximate snapshots); the other 44 keep their earlier dated values.
New report: Twenty-fifth check (24 Oct 2026), with the re-check of 31 grades, fly-chess's shuffled-wiring control, two new entries, three ledger rows, neural-canvas in our browser and limits.

Relays (pre-registered, brain only; the 13 Oct headline and 15 Oct lines unchanged): 23 Oct: our earlier controls matched each relay neuron's activity, but not how strongly it connects to the turn neuron. This time the control is a group of other active neurons that excite the turn neuron, chosen so that together they fire about as much as the active relays and send about as many synapses to the turn neuron (both within 20%). Left eye: in 1 of 5 matched groups the turn neuron's rate fell as low as, or lower than, with the relays silenced (matched groups 13-31 Hz, relays 16.0 Hz, nothing silenced 21-25 Hz). By our pre-registered rule, this test does not show that the relays matter more than other inputs with the same combined connection strength and activity. Right eye: among the 9 other active neurons that excite the turn neuron, no group came within 20% of the relays on both combined activity and synapse count (we had set 5 groups as the minimum in advance), so this control could not be built for this eye. Our rule compares the relays with the lowest matched group, so extra groups can only make the relays look less special, never more. Left eye: outside the stimulated looming neurons, the brain fired 13,581-14,040 spikes with a matched group silenced, against 13,901-14,760 with the relays silenced and 14,502-15,172 with nothing silenced. One model, brain only, one stimulus strength (80 spikes/s), 5 matched groups on the left eye only, each run once; the 5 groups all share the same three most active neurons, so they are not independent draws; not a real fly.
23 Oct: we re-checked the 28 projects we last graded between 29 Sep and 5 Oct against their current code: 27 keep their grade (5 after a full re-read); 1 more will be re-checked in the next run.

200 catalogue entries (23 Oct 2026): 3 new: drosophila-connectome-sim A (helps): from the author's committed control file (20 trials per arm; not re-run by us), sugar input drove the feeding motor neuron MN9 at 67.45 Hz on the real FlyWire weights and at 0.0 Hz in every trial of all 10 weight-shuffled brains; no no-brain baseline reported, no chance level. fly-brain-resuscitation A (worse): from the author's committed structure results (one rewired copy, not re-run by us), sensory-to-motor reachability in the real wiring collapsed after removing 3.5% of neurons in order of connectivity, against 26.6% in a degree-preserving rewired copy; we read a higher critical fraction as a sturdier network; the author does not present it as a score; no no-brain baseline applies to this structural measure and it has no chance level. owen-silva-fly-brain A (worse): from the author's pre-registered results (20 seeds; not re-run by us), the mushroom-body model on the real wiring reached 57.5% final accuracy over 110 odours, against 64.4% with shuffled and 66.8% with uniform wiring; no no-brain baseline is reported and chance is about 0.9%. connectomics-fly-whole-brain-nulls: The repository was no longer online on 22 and 23 Oct 2026; the grade and the numbers describe the code we read on 21 Oct. Its link status is now gone; grade A of 21 Oct and its ledger row stay. maxwells-demon-fly-brain: the test good:bad crossing ratio was 0.645 for the real wiring, 0.597 for the shuffled wiring and 1.035 for random decisions, the no-brain baseline, and higher is better by the author's write-up (the code computes the ratio; the README does not say), so random decisions scored above both wirings. flybench keeps A at its current version (v1.0.0, commit 56577bf); its measured result moved by about 0.01. Odyssey-3 claim: No method, code or write-up was published as of 23 Oct 2026.

Controls ledger (23 Oct 2026): 7 new rows (3 new entries; flywire-connectome-scz-step68 (no difference): real wiring 0.575 against 0.589 for random wiring that keeps each Kenyon cell's input strength (median of 10); chance 0.053; flywire-connectome-scz-step69 (no difference): real wiring 0.954 against 0.959 for random wiring (median of 10); no no-brain baseline reported; fly-connectome-study-v4-stage7 (mixed): real 0.349, shuffled 0.332, random 0.329; raw responses without a Kenyon-cell layer 0.351; chance about 0.11; fly-connectome-study-v4-stage3b (mixed): real 0.650, input-total control 0.648, random 0.628; no no-brain baseline reported), now 91 studies, 81 with a wiring null: helps 32, no difference 23, worse 8, mixed 15, not yet scored 3; fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 32 of 81. Scoring unchanged.

On 23 Oct 2026 the short requirements.txt command picked 6 newer packages than our exact lock, including python-dateutil 3.0.0, a new major version; the six main packages are pinned and did not change. We have tested only the exact lock. The next beginner re-test stays due 2 Nov 2026.

Tracking (23 Oct 2026): repositories of 142 catalogue entries checked; 56 of 56 videos available. View counts were not refreshed on 23 Oct 2026 (YouTube search pages could not be read); every count keeps its earlier date.
New report: Twenty-fourth check (23 Oct 2026), with a group-matched control for the relays, the re-check of 28 grades, three new entries, seven ledger rows and limits.

22 Oct: we re-checked the 34 projects we last graded on 28 Sep against their current code: 33 keep their grade (3 of them after a full re-read of changed code), and 1 could not be re-checked because the source is no longer online. Re-read in full after code changes, grades kept: flyvis A, flydoom-mutkuoz A and fly-dino C. Not re-checkable: flydoom (its repository is no longer online; grade C and its date unchanged).

197 catalogue entries (22 Oct 2026): 2 new: matcha-fly A: From the author's pre-registered looming-escape experiment (10 seeds; not re-run by us), driving the looming detectors gave 241.7 giant-fibre spikes on the real wiring, while the highest of 100 shuffled-wiring brains reached 21.0; no no-brain baseline is reported and a spike count has no chance level, and driving random sets of other visual neurons instead gave 2.0 to 18.7 spikes. maxwells-demon-fly-brain A: In the author's benchmark (3 seeds, reported by the author; not re-run by us), the test good:bad crossing ratio was 0.645 for the real wiring, 0.597 for the shuffled wiring and 1.035 for random decisions, the no-brain baseline. The author's files do not state whether a higher ratio is better; we read higher as better, and on that reading random decisions scored above both wirings. fly-connectome-study stays A at its current commit (the author's numbers, not re-run by us): in the author's planted positive control, real minus shuffled wiring was +0.064 [+0.058, +0.071] and real minus random wiring +0.066 [+0.059, +0.074], while the no-brain linear readout was level with the real wiring at −0.004 [−0.008, +0.001]. fly-with-me stays B: the brain still runs the Shiu et al. model on FlyWire v783 with hand-made ear bands and dance moves, and there is no wiring comparison; the author reports a trained brain at 0.498 macro-F1 against 0.485 for the ear input alone (difference +0.013 ± 0.028; the results file is not in the repository). FlyGateDemo stays A: we read the code behind its loader, its wiring comparison and its no-brain cosine baseline; its numbers are reported in the README, printed by the author's program, and were not re-run by us. adfly-connectome: links now point at the current commit (the earlier commit is gone; code and results unchanged), and the claim cites the authors' arXiv preprint (arXiv:2610.19153, 13 Oct 2026); grade B unchanged. Odyssey-3 claim: No method, code or write-up was published as of 22 Oct 2026.

Controls ledger (22 Oct 2026): 2 new rows (matcha-fly helps, maxwells-demon-fly-brain no difference), now 84 studies, 74 with a wiring null: helps 31, no difference 21, worse 6, mixed 13, not yet scored 3; fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 31 of 74. Scoring unchanged.

neural-canvas: 22 Oct: in a headless browser without a GPU, after we pressed 'Download & start', the page prepared its scene for about 73 seconds, then started a background worker, which downloaded about 79 MB within about 94 seconds of the click; the picture changed between our later screenshots, and at the end of our about 187-second watch the page's status line read 'JavaScript · 0.02× realtime · 0 spikes'. Screenshots cannot show whether the brain drives the movement. Status: loads; brain simulation not seen in our headless browser without a GPU (checked 2026-10-22). Correction: On 6 and 20 Oct our check pressed 'Download & start'; in the about 30 seconds we watched afterwards, the page fetched about 6 MB and started no background worker, and our screenshots show only the start card and a loading screen.

Tracking (22 Oct 2026): repositories of 141 catalogue entries checked; 56 of 56 videos available. 14 gallery videos have view counts read on 22 Oct 2026 and 3 on 21 Oct 2026 (approximate, from YouTube search results pages, linked on each card).
New report: Twenty-third check (22 Oct 2026), with the four-week re-check of 34 grades, two new entries and ledger rows, a longer neural-canvas watch, re-checks and limits.
